title: Assignment 5: Drive Forward and Stop with ROS 2
description: Create a ROS 2 velocity publisher that moves a robot forward and then stops safely.
assignment_html:
Scenario

Purpose: Create a ROS 2 node that moves a robot straight forward for a fixed time and then continuously commands a safe stop.

You are programming a mobile robot in ROS 2. The robot receives movement commands through the /cmd_vel topic.

File and editing rule

Read the complete project tree, but edit only:

src/robot_motion/robot_motion/controller.py

Do not rename the package, node, executable, topic, class, methods, or starter variables.

ROS 2 primer

  • A node is one running ROS program. Here it is the RobotController class, which extends rclpy.node.Node; super().__init__('robot_controller') gives the node its name.
  • A package groups nodes with their build files. package.xml lists dependencies, setup.py registers the controller executable, and the launch file starts the node. These files are supplied and read-only.
  • main() calls rclpy.init(), creates the node, and calls rclpy.spin(node), which keeps the node alive and runs its callbacks until it is stopped.
  • self.create_publisher(Twist, '/cmd_vel', 10) returns a publisher, and publisher.publish(message) sends one message on that topic.
  • self.create_timer(0.1, self.control_robot) asks ROS to call control_robot every 0.1 seconds.
  • Twist() creates a velocity message with every field set to 0.0. Set fields such as command.linear.x = 0.20 before publishing.
  • Run Tests builds the package with colcon build, starts the node, and records what it publishes on /cmd_vel.

ROS terms

  • A publisher sends a message to a named topic; a subscriber receives messages from a topic.
  • A callback is a function ROS calls when an event happens. Here, the event is a timer tick every 0.1 seconds.
  • Queue depth 10 is the communication history setting, not the number of movement commands to send.
  • Twist.linear.x is forward speed in meters per second; Twist.angular.z is turning speed in radians per second.

Keep the supplied communication settings. Grading observes messages and counts publications inside completed callbacks; it is not a physical robot safety certification or a static check of every scaffold name.

Task

  1. Create a geometry_msgs/msg/Twist publisher on /cmd_vel with queue depth 10.
  2. On each 0.1-second timer callback, create and publish one Twist command.
  3. While elapsed_time is less than 5.0 seconds, set linear.x to 0.20 m/s and angular.z to 0.0 rad/s.
  4. At and after 5.0 seconds, publish zero linear and angular velocity. elapsed_time counts timer callbacks, and 0.1 cannot be stored exactly as a float, so the switch may happen one callback after 5.0 seconds. The grader's 0.5-second tolerance allows this.
  5. Keep the node running and continue publishing zero velocity after stopping.

Safety requirements

  • The robot must move forward without turning.
  • Ending the program is not a safe stop; the node must explicitly publish zero velocity.
  • Every timer callback must publish exactly one command.

What Run Tests checks

  • The package builds and the node starts.
  • Exactly one Twist command is published on /cmd_vel per timer callback, at a sufficient rate.
  • Forward and angular speeds match the required behavior.
  • The robot stops after approximately five seconds and remains stopped.

No robot simulator is used in this assignment.

How scoring works

Building and starting are worth 20%, but because the package and node are supplied, this credit counts only after your code passes at least one behavior check. The untouched starter earns 0%. The remaining checks award 20% for publishing, 20% for forward speed, 10% for straight motion, 20% for stopping on time, and 10% for holding the stop. Straight motion earns credit only when the robot also drives forward at the required speed; a node that never moves does not earn it. Stop timing is measured from the first observed command with a 0.5-second tolerance; launch time is not extra driving time.

def main(args=None):
    rclpy.init(args=args)
    controller = RobotController()
    try:

learning_objectives: Create a ROS 2 publisher with rclpy.
Use a timer callback to control robot motion over time.
Stop a mobile robot by continuously publishing zero velocity.

rubric.description: The package builds and the node starts.
Publishes the required forward velocity without rotation.
Stops at the required time and holds zero velocity.

common_misconceptions.description: The publisher was not created or uses the wrong topic.
Linear or angular velocity was assigned to the wrong Twist field.
The robot moves correctly but never publishes a stop command.

solution_html:
Approach

  1. Create a Twist publisher for /cmd_vel.
  2. Publish linear.x = 0.20 and angular.z = 0.0 during the movement period.
  3. After five seconds, publish zero for both values and continue publishing the stopped state.
